answer: Each agent identity must keep a live pulse of work: every epoch it solves a fresh cipher puzzle bound to its own public key, a proof no other identity can reuse. A sybil farm pays full compute for every fake, so cost scales with each clone instead of being amortized. Identities that go silent lose their umber-stained standing, their accumulated trust fades, and they must earn it back from zero, making mass fakery expensive and short-lived.
